titulo: Rebuilding CI for AI-Scale Commit Volume — Gautam Korlam, Sonar
descripcion_recortada: A coding agent can produce changes faster than the queues that test, review and merge them. Gautam Korlam examines that mismatch through his work on Uber's SubmitQueue and Gitar, now part of Sonar. A merge queue keeps the main branch healthy by testing combinations of changes before they land, but a process designed for human arrival rates can become a bottleneck when agents create many pull requests at once. Faster code generation shifts the constraint to failed builds, repeated repairs, review and approvals. Korlam argues that the engineering system around the agent must change alongside the agent itself. The talk follows those constraints through CI and the merge path. Incremental builds, caching, sharding and parallel work reduce the cost of repeated feedback; a Rust example illustrates the difference between rebuilding everything and testing the affected work. Agents also need durable context from logs and failures so a repair loop does not repeatedly rediscover the same problem.
